panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Axial T1-weighted MRI of mid-thigh, distal thigh and mid-calf in a patient with IBM showing intramuscular fat accumulation (hyperintensity) most notably in the quadriceps with asymmetric hamstring involvement and calf medial gastrocnemius/soleus fat replacement; the caption explicitly labels this as typical IBM MRI appearance. b: Axial T1-weighted MRI of the mid-thigh of the same IBM patient six years later showing clear progression of quadriceps intramuscular fat accumulation with relative biceps femoris sparing; classic longitudinal IBM MRI. c: Axial STIR MRI of distal thigh and mid-calf in the same IBM patient showing acute muscle inflammation as hyperintensity (muscle edema) most markedly in the vastus medialis and soleus; a real patient IBM image with a specific inflammatory manifestation, but no vocabulary key exists for STIR muscle edema, so it is recorded as a proposed finding.

panels.figure_caption: Typical MRI appearances in a patient with IBM. (a) Axial T1-weighted images of the mid-thigh (top), distal thigh (middle), and mid-calf (bottom). The thigh shows intramuscular fat accumulation, evident as hyperintensity; most notably within the quadriceps (RF: rectus femoris; VL: vastus lateralis; VM: vastus medialis), especially in the distal thigh. Hamstring involvement is asymmetric, with semimembranosus (SM) relatively spared on the left. In the calf the medial gastrocnemius (MG) is completely replaced by fat, with the soleus (So) also severely affected. (b) Axial T1-weighted image at mid-thigh of the same patient six years later shows significant progression of intramuscular fat accumulation, with only the biceps femoris (BF) relatively unaffected. (c) Axial STIR images at distal thigh (top) and mid-calf (calf) in the same patient at baseline. Acute muscle inflammation is evident as hyperintensity, most markedly in the vastus medialis and soleus

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of a patient with inclusion body myositis showing the classic bilateral quadriceps muscle atrophy, which is a hallmark clinical feature of IBM. The caption explicitly states this is muscle atrophy in the bilateral quadriceps in a patient with IBM, matching the finding_key for marked quadriceps wasting. B: Clinical photograph of a patient with inclusion body myositis showing bilateral forearm muscle atrophy and weakness in hand grip and finger flexion. Finger flexor weakness with forearm wasting is a classic and hallmark clinical feature of IBM, directly matching the finding_key for asymmetric finger flexor wasting.

in_text_mentions: Representative images of histological and immunohistochemical findings of the sIBM cases are shown in Figures 2 and 3. All sIBM biopsies showed preservation of the fiber-typing distribution pattern, variation in size of the fibers, presence of rimmed vacuoles (except biopsies 1a, 4a, 7a, and 12a), increased nuclear internalization, endomysial inflammatory infiltration, increased reaction to acid phosphatase, and unspecific changes at oxidative stains. Just over half of the biopsies showed reduced labeling for COX or COX-negative fibers. Four biopsies had RRF, and ten showed SDH-positive fibers

All sIBM and inflammatory myopathy control cases showed increased labeling for inflammatory markers (CD4, CD8, CD68, and MHC-I) (Figures 3(a) and 3(b)/Table 5). There was increased expression of LC3B (autophagic marker), especially in the vacuoles, in 67% of sIBM cases (n = 12) (Figure 3(c)). The expression was not increased in cases 6, 9, 12, 14, 17, and 18, as well as in the controls (cases 19, 20, 21, 22, and 23). The expression of p62/SQSTM1 (anti-p62) was positive in all cases of sIBM (Figure 3(f)). Expression of α-synuclein staining was positive in about 89% of sIBM cases (Figure 3(d)).

panels.rationale: H&E section of left calf muscle from a patient with sporadic inclusion body myositis showing endomysial inflammation and myofiber dystrophy at 40x; prior caption triage confirms diagnostic histopathology in a real sIBM patient. The image shows classic IBM features: dense endomysial mononuclear infiltrate, fiber size variation, and vacuolated fibers with granular rims; a yellow arrow annotates the abnormal area. Disease attribution is supported by the disease-focused article title (COVID-19-Induced Sporadic Inclusion Body Myositis) and the specific captioned manifestation. [raw subtype: sporadic]
